title: Mexico’s Bank of Wellbeing Launches App for Transfers and Digital Payments Without Fees
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [November 12, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/banco-del-bienestar-
lanza-aplicacion-para-transferencias-y-pagos-digitales-sin-comisiones/), an
investigative Mexican news outlet._

The **Banco del Bienestar** developed a **mobile app** so that beneficiaries
of social programs can make transfers, send and receive money, as well as
**make and receive digital payments** from their cellphones, **without paying
fees** , its director general, **Víctor Manuel Lamoyi Bocanegra** , announced.

The new tool will allow users to “send and receive money free of charge,
without fees —as always—, make transfers to other accounts, send money using a
cellphone number and also make and receive digital payments using a **QR
code** ,” the official explained during its presentation at the presidential
press conference.

He indicated that the previous app, available since 2022, only allowed users
to check balances and transactions. That tool reached **18 million users** and
handled more than one million inquiries a day, which helped reduce waiting
times at branches and ATMs.

Given those results, the new platform is projected to reach up to **43 million
users** and, according to the bank’s director, seeks to expand the options for
people to use their funds without having to go to a branch or withdraw cash.

He emphasized that the Banco del Bienestar has more than **3,100 branches in
2,705 localities across 1,972 municipalities**. **In more than 1,000
municipalities, it is the only banking institution with a presence** , which
allows it to serve communities where commercial banks do not operate.

In 2026, the institution will have served 42.8 million beneficiaries of **29
well-being programs** and disbursed **one trillion pesos** , equivalent to one
million million, in pensions, scholarships and other federal government
assistance.

The programs whose funds it distributes include pensions for older adults,
women and people with disabilities; the **Rita Cetina, Gertrudis Bocanegra and
Jóvenes Escribiendo el Futuro** scholarships, as well as assistance for
working mothers, agriculture, fishing, housing, health and food.

Lamoyi Bocanegra noted that the bank serves more than 500,000 people daily at
its branches and ATMs, and has close to **3,000 ATMs operating 24 hours a
day**. In addition, its Contact Center receives more than 16,000 calls and
handles up to 480,000 balance inquiries a day.

The director general added that the new app is the bank’s first digital
payment service aligned with the **Law on the Digital Economy and Digital and
Electronic Payments** , recently published in the **Official Gazette of the
Federation.**

With this tool, he maintained, the institution seeks to expand beneficiaries’
access to digital financial services and offer alternatives for directly
managing and using funds from social programs.
